# Exact routed 245 register-program decoder

The routed 245 candidate uses different instruction addresses from the original
254-state compiler. `ProgramRouting245` now has a checked decoder for the new
addresses, with the original pointer-consumption and register effects preserved.
Its 203 stored subtrees expand to 6,459 internal nodes, 6,460 leaves, depth 51
and exactly one halt leaf. The storage count is distinct from the candidate's
245 binary states and its 128 routing-grammar roles.

[`ProgramRouting245.lean`](../../Lean/BusyBeaver/ZFC/ProgramRouting245.lean)
proves the exact source/tree identity for every decoder fuel at least 51, then
uses the normal program fuel 204. `walk_eq_tree` covers arbitrary pointers and
read positions. `step_eq_tree` applies to every register function, retaining
`RegisterPath.consume`, increment, both decrement outcomes, break and continue.
The 203 private row equalities and 203 private subtree identities are dependencies
of the public proofs; the [audit](program_routing245_audit.lean) prints 11 public
axiom reports and checks 13 typed callers.

The input is the exact
[logical-site certificate](../../../../SetTheory/Cardinals/docs/reports/set-theory/zfc-closure-kernels/data/68-route245-certificate-sites_logical.json)
from arrival `8286787dd0`, SHA-256
`f77a3fb9729382a0b8cd24d480639862b63ecb76bbc205542d1fc7077c025745`.
The source emitter separately parses its rendered rows and checks their complete
unfolding against all ordered paths and operands. All 6,460 operations and
arguments match the original program order; 6,241 addresses change. This finite
comparison is separate from the remaining proof of halting equivalence with
`Prog254`.

The [actual run3 record](results/program-routing245-verification.json) reports a
complete source/audit PASS: source 6.033798 seconds, audit 0.283444 seconds, zero
warnings. Six public probes use no axioms, three use `propext`, and two use
`propext` with `Quot.sound`. The actual fresh source object was recorded before
the audit and remained unchanged afterward. The
[independent review](results/program-routing245-review.json) examines the final
evidence without replaying it.

The [lossless text history](results/program-routing245-history.json) preserves
the initial drafts, all three execution records, exact guard/source/audit versions,
preparations, reviews, repairs and logs. Run1 failed in two final source wrappers.
Run2 passed the repaired source but failed two concrete audit rewrites. Run3 kept
that successful source byte-identical and repaired the two audit proof bodies.
The earlier failures remain separate records; their printed standard axioms are
not presented as complete successful audits.

The [guard](check_program_routing245.py) selects exactly `RegisterPath`, `RMDag`,
`RMEquiv` and `RMBisim` from the checked
[BinaryPrefix246 parent](results/prefix246-binary-verification.json), plus the
toolchain `Init` boundary. It records 20 inputs, exact first providers, snapshots
and postchecks. Source and audit share 120 seconds, with `-j1 -M4096` and default
proof limits. No dependency build, download or compiler-version query occurs.
The historical compiled providers and recorded compiler are required; this is
not a clean-checkout build or a dependency-reconstruction claim.

```sh
python3 Computability/BusyBeaver/Research/ZFC/check_program_routing245.py --repo "$PWD" --output /tmp/program-routing245-prepared --prepare-only
python3 Computability/BusyBeaver/Research/ZFC/check_program_routing245.py --repo "$PWD" --output /tmp/program-routing245-check
```

The portable guard changes path defaults only. All proof and metadata hashes
remain those of run3. The exact executed
[emitter](program-routing245/provenance/prepare_source.py),
[inventory](program-routing245/source-inventory.json),
[parsed data](program-routing245/program-data.json) and
[provider boundary](program-routing245/dependency-boundary-plan.json) remain
byte-identical; the inventory's emitter hash continues to bind the original
emitter. It retains historical paths and is preserved as provenance.

This unit establishes the new register decoder and its full one-step leaf
semantics. It does not yet establish source bisimulation, binary-machine
simulation, blank initialization, a consistency equivalence, or PA
internalization. In particular, the separate checked 246-state endpoint does not
automatically transfer to the new program.

Attribution remains with Mira-Cult for the original machine/calculus, Jeff
Ketchersid for public verification, Andrew James Wade for the compiler framework,
and the routed-245 submission and prior ProveIt contributions. The original
notices and candidate attribution are retained in the
[candidate documentation](candidate-routing245/README.md).
